svg.title: Auto Switch — one complete circuit
svg.desc: A continuous schematic of every external harness connection. All grounds join the bottom return bus. Wire crossings with a white gap are not connected; filled dots are junctions. The Pico internal USB and 3.3 volt power path is shown inside its board outline.

g.title: GND: BAT.black, MASTER.GND, REG.GND, GATE.GND, PICO.pin38_GND, SERVO0.ground, SERVO1.ground, D2.anode, C1.negative, R_BOTTOM.2, C_ADC.2, R_EN.2, R_BLEED.2
SERVO_5V: GATE.VOUT, SERVO0.power, SERVO1.power, D2.cathode, R_BLEED.1

svg.text: Every wire drawn. Follow battery power across the top, signals through the middle, and the common return along the bottom.
● Joined wires White gap at a crossing = not connected Pad numbers are physical Pico pads, not GPIO numbers
Orange: raw battery · Red: regulated / motor power · Purple: Pico supply · Blue: control · Teal: sensing · Gray: ground
40 · VBUS and 36 · 3V3 OUT: no harness wire
* Verify colors on your actual servo.
Servo 1 + R_PWM1 omitted for one switch.
COMMON GND — one continuous return. Motor current returns here directly; it does not pass through the Pico.
External D1 feeds VSYS. USB feeds VSYS through the Pico’s own diode. USB alone cannot power this servo branch.
C1 is BEFORE the gate. D2 and R_BLEED are AFTER it. All values match harness revision 3.
Electrical topology, not physical board placement. Check silkscreen, diode/capacitor polarity and continuity before powering the assembly.
